full_judgment:
3. The defendant respondent No.1 appeared in the suit and filed an application under order VII Rule 11 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint on the ground that the said suit was hopelessly barred by the limitation. 

 4. The learned Joint District Judge, Khulna, by an order dated 28.01.2018, rejected the said application for rejection of the plaint holding that the suit was barred by limitation or not should be decided after recording evidence. Against the said order, the defendant No.1 filed civil revisional application in the High Court Division and obtained Rule. The High Curt Division, by the impugned judgment and order, made the said Rule absolute and rejected the plaint of the aforesaid title suit. Thus, the plaintiff has filed this civil petition for leave to appeal. 

 5. Mr. Ahmed Nowshad ,Tamil, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that the instant suit was barred by limitation or not is a mixed question of law and fact, the High Court Division has committed-error of law in rejecting the plaint holding that the suit was barred by limitation. He further submits that the plaint, the original agreement for sale and subsequent payment of consideration of money by executing receipts and surrounding circumstances clearly indicate that the instant suit was not barred by limitation, the High Court Division erred in law in rejecting the plaint. 

 6. Mr. Shardar Abul Hossain, learned Advocate appearing for the respondent, submits that the instant suit was hopelessly barred by limitation, the High Court Division upon proper appreciation of contents of the plaint rightly held so land, thereby, rejected the plaint. 

 8. For the limited purpose of determining the question whether the suit is to be wiped out under order VII Rule 11 C.P.C. or not the averments in the plaint are only to be looked into. Only the contents of the plaint are germane. The suit could not be dismissed as barred by limitation without framing of issue on limitation and taking evidence. Question of limitation is a mixed question of fact, and law and on ex-facie reading of the plaint it could not be held that the suit was barred by limitation. The averments of the plaint have to be read as a whole. 

 9. It is positive case of the plaintiff that executing subsequent payment receipts the defendant No.1 extended the time for execution and registration of sale deed and he has filed the instant suit within the stipulated time of limitation. The limitation, as provided under Article 113 of the Limitation Act started depending upon the facts and circumstances of the as well as the contents of the agreement for sale and subsequent money receipts. It is unsafe to draw conclusion before recording evidence to ascertain starting point of limitation. Since the power conferred on the court to terminate civil action at the threshold is drastic, the conditions enumerated under Order VII Rule 11 C.P.C. to the exercise of rejection of the plaint to be strictly adhered to. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the matter, we are of the view that the High Court Division has committed error of law in rejecting the plaint holding that the instant suit was barred by limitation. The trial Court rightly observed that an issue is to be framed in deciding the point of limitation, that is, as to whether the instant suit was barred by limitation or not. 

 12. The judgment and order dated 19.09.2021 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 854 of 2018 is hereby set aside. The trial Court is directed to frame an issue as to whether the suit is barred by limitation or not and, thereafter dispose of the suit in accordance with law.
